interpretations.rationale: The authority-transition signal is unstable and does not recover in this run. Receipt 19867c5d7a784ca8afcec5890786dba3 ran decided_stopsign_flips_through_reconnect_sync (exit 0, test passed). Event 0 (ready) records node 5 at decided 5 with is_reconfigured true and node 2 at decided 4 with accepted 5, so the StopSign was decided on node 5 while the future leader's quorum had not decided it. Event 1 (after_sync) records decided 4 and is_reconfigured false; the single declared comparison (reconfig eq true at phase after_sync) is complete and violated, which is the flip. Event 2 (after_redecide) records decided 5 with decided_leader2 5 but is_reconfigured still false. With the StopSign still stored, is_reconfigured being false at decided 5 means the accepted index is no longer 5, and the source shows why: sync_log sets accepted to sync.sync_idx + suffix length and then adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign, even though node 5's accepted prefix already included that StopSign (sync_idx was 5). The sync therefore lowers decided below the accepted StopSign and also advances accepted past the log's last index, so decided can never catch up and the reconfiguration never reads as decided again on that node. A user polling is_reconfigured sees a decided reconfiguration revert to not-decided indefinitely on this follower after a reconnect, while the rest of the cluster re-decides. The exact accepted value and whether any later sync repairs it are not yet measured, so they are recorded as a gap and the successor adds accepted to the sample.

The StopSign value is preserved and the rest of the cluster re-decides index 5, so this is a status/authority-signal defect, not loss of the reconfiguration or divergence of values.
Whether the accepted index mismatch is permanent or repaired by a later sync is unmeasured; the third event suggests it persists through the re-decision.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.

investigations.question: Can a StopSign that a node already observed as decided become undecided again after a reconnect AcceptSync from a leader with a lower decided index, so is_reconfigured() flips Some -> None -> Some?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. stopsign_is_decided is decided_idx == accepted_idx, and is_reconfigured returns Some only while that holds. sync_log assigns the new leader's decided index unconditionally, so a node that had decided its accepted StopSign (decided == accepted) and then applies an AcceptSync carrying a lower decided index keeps the StopSign accepted but no longer decided. is_reconfigured therefore returns None until the new leader re-decides the StopSign, after which it returns Some again.

knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor, append_notify tracking enabled; pending entry has an assigned (idx, ballot) from local accept or a remote Assigned reply; drain_notifiers runs on each actor tick and after command handling.

knowledge.statement: The runtime's test suite treats a successful append_notify as a claim that the caller's entry is decided at the returned index: the batching regression test reads the decided log back and asserts the value at the returned index equals the submitted entry, so a returned index holding a different value is a contract violation under the project's own expectation.
knowledge.conditions: The test environment's exercised conditions: 3-node runtime cluster with real transport, batching enabled, and a submitted append_notify entry; this is an individual test expectation plus the handle-level description, not a proof of a defect by itself.

knowledge.statement: A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum (handle_majority_promises -> get_max_decided_idx). A follower whose Promise arrives after that quorum is answered by handle_promise_accept with send_accsync stamped with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which assigns it to the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that had already learned a later decision therefore loses decided progress until the new leader re-accepts and re-decides the entry.

knowledge.statement: Entries appended while this node is leader in Phase::Prepare are pushed to buffered_proposals. When the node later receives an AcceptSync (after promising a leader, whether in the prepare phase or in the accept phase), handle_acceptsync calls forward_buffered_proposals before switching to Phase::Accept; that call takes the whole buffer and forwards it to the current leader if there is no accepted StopSign. The buffered entries are therefore re-proposed rather than stranded when leadership moves away before the prepare quorum completes.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::snapshot passes its index to InternalStorage::try_snapshot, which accepts any index less than the local decided index (equal maps to the decided index without the StopSign) and rejects only indices greater than decided with UndecidedIndex. It performs trim, compacted-index and snapshot writes atomically and never consults the minimum accepted index. The snapshot API is therefore not affected by the sparse-pid placeholders that block trim, so a snapshot-capable Entry type can still compact a configuration such as {1,2,5}.
knowledge.conditions: A snapshot-capable Entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) and a snapshot index not greater than the node's decided index; the node may be a follower when local_only is true.

What is not yet established is the decisive schedule: the origin's actor drains on each tick (10 ms by default) and when commands arrive, so a drain while decided_idx < assigned_idx and the promise ballot has already changed yields Superseded and avoids the false Ok. interpretations.rationale: The pending completion path can report a false success, under a schedule the actor does not exclude. A pending append_notify keeps only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot). drain_notifiers evaluates, in order, Ok when assigned_idx <= decided, then Superseded when the assignment ballot is below the current promise ballot, then Timeout; the Ok arm reads no log entry and never checks that the value at assigned_idx is the caller's entry. The origin can hold an assignment made when it was leader or when a leader accepted its proposal, lose leadership to a higher ballot, and then have its own decided index advance past assigned_idx with a different value at that index: the runtime's own Superseded regression test constructs exactly that replacement (the old leader accepts locally with its outgoing cut, a new leader appends a fresh entry that decides at the same index, and the origin learns of the new ballot). Whether the pending resolves Ok or Superseded then depends only on whether a drain runs after the promise advanced but before decided reached assigned_idx. drain_notifiers runs only in the actor's tick branch; handling an incoming message never drains. Nothing orders a tick between the ballot change and the decided advance, so when the origin processes the higher-ballot Prepare and then the message that carries decided >= assigned_idx within one tick interval, the Ok arm wins and the caller is told its entry is decided at an index that holds a different entry. With a legal user-set tick_period that exceeds the leadership-turnover interval, that ordering is deterministic; with a short period it is a race. The gap on the reachable schedule is therefore answered on source grounds: no mechanism prevents it, and a legal configuration makes it the expected ordering.

3f84facd1a81451882518e32ee8be535-gap-0.explanation: Reachable. drain_notifiers is invoked only from the tick branch (actor.rs tick handling), while handle_incoming_tracked processes messages without draining; the actor polls the tick first each iteration but the tick fires at most once per configured period. The ballot change (Prepare/AcceptSync from the new leader) and the decided advance (AcceptDecide/Decide from that leader) are separate messages that can both be processed inside one period. If the period exceeds the turnover interval, the pending sees decided >= assigned_idx and a stale assignment ballot at the same drain, and the Ok arm precedes the Superseded arm. Since tick_period is user-set and only advised to match the ServerConfig tick budget, this ordering is legal and deterministic in that configuration.

The Superseded doc already calls the error a heuristic and tells callers to inspect the index, which mitigates the Superseded path but not a false Ok.

The false Ok needs the caller's entry to have been accepted without a majority and then replaced at the same index; if the entry is adopted by the new leader, Ok is correct.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes the mechanism but not yet the witness. handle_majority_promises sets the new leader's decided index to the maximum decided among the promises it has received (the prepare quorum); send_accsync then stamps every later promiser's AcceptSync with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which sets the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that promised during the prepare phase is part of that maximum; a follower whose Prepare is delayed until the leader is already in Accept is not, and set_promise for that later promise is called with check_max_prom false and does not update the maximum. If that follower had already learned a decision the quorum members had not, the AcceptSync lowers its decided index and read() reports a previously Decided entry as Undecided, contradicting the documented guarantee that a decided entry is not reverted and is safe to apply. The new leader then re-accepts and re-decides the entry after its accept quorum acknowledges, so the entry returns to Decided, exposing an at-least-once application hazard. The decisive uncertainty is whether the state can be built with real instances and legal message delays, which the registered five-node probe measures.
counterevidence: If the delayed follower's promise reaches the leader before the prepare quorum completes, its decided index participates in the maximum and no regression occurs.
If every member of the new leader's prepare quorum has also received the earlier Decide, the leader's decided index already covers the entry and the sync is not lowering anything.
The value of the entry is preserved by the sync, so this is a visibility and application-status defect rather than a divergence of decided values.

interpretations.rationale: This experiment shows the fan-out consequence of the decided-stream defect and extends the earlier single-subscriber witness, which remains in its own interpretation. Receipt 149052bc9a0d495985d41bd165deada3 ran fanout_skips_entries_for_fast_subscriber_with_lagging_peer (exit 0, test passed); its declared comparison (fast_stream eq 10,8,9,10) is complete and holds, evaluating event 1. Event 0 fixes the setup: decided 10, compacted 5, trailing cursor 1, fast cursor 6. Event 1 reports slow_stream T5,6,7,8,9,10,8,9,10 and fast_stream 10,8,9,10 with both cursors ending at 10. The slow subscriber re-receives 8,9,10 because its cursor advanced one step per element while the marker stood for indices 1-4. The fast subscriber is worse: push_to_all_subs reads from the trailing cursor 1, so the collapsed marker shifts every later element by compacted-1-min_next = 3 positions, and start = 6-1 = 5 lands on the last element, entry 10. The fast subscriber therefore receives entry 10 where it expected entry 7, then receives 8,9,10 on the next round; entry 7 is never delivered and entry 10 is delivered twice. Because the actor treats each pushed element as one committed log position, a single lagging subscriber silently corrupts the decided stream of every other subscriber. The root cause is the same as the earlier witness: the core read collapses a trimmed prefix into one element while the actor advances cursors and offsets fan-out by log index. A subscriber stream that silently omits a committed entry is a stronger violation of the documented in-order decided stream than duplicate delivery, and an application applying entries from the stream would miss entry 7 permanently.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?

knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor, append_notify tracking enabled; pending entry has an assigned (idx, ballot) from local accept or a remote Assigned reply; drain_notifiers runs on each actor tick and after command handling.

interpretations.rationale: The source establishes the mechanism: a pending append_notify stores only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot), and drain_notifiers resolves Ok whenever decided_idx >= assigned_idx before it checks whether that ballot has been superseded; nothing in the Ok path reads the entry at assigned_idx. The runtime's own tests establish both premises the false Ok would need: Ok(idx) is expected to mean the caller's value is decided at idx, and an entry accepted only on the old leader can be replaced at the same index by a different decided value while the origin learns of the new ballot. What is not yet established is the decisive schedule: the origin's actor drains on each tick (10 ms by default) and when commands arrive, so a drain while decided_idx < assigned_idx and the promise ballot has already changed yields Superseded and avoids the false Ok. A false Ok requires the decided advance to assigned_idx and the ballot change to be visible in the same drain pass, or the decided advance to arrive with the new ballot before any intervening tick. The runtime crate is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos test target, so the fixed assurance_generated harness cannot execute this path; the open question is therefore the actor-level interleaving and log-content identity, not the core Paxos decision rule.
counterevidence: The Superseded doc explicitly calls itself a heuristic and notes the entry can still be decided under the new ballot at log_entry_idx; when the caller's entry survives reconciliation, returning Ok once decided_idx reaches idx is correct and must not be suppressed.

The false-Ok case requires the origin's own minority-accepted entry to be replaced at that index; if the new leader adopts the value, the decided entry at idx is still the caller's entry and Ok is accurate.
limitations: omnipaxos_runtime is not listed in omnipaxos/Cargo.toml dev-dependencies, so tests/assurance_generated.rs in the omnipaxos crate cannot construct the actor or call append_notify.
No execution receipt exists for this question; the account rests on source reading and the runtime's saved test expectations, which describe intent but do not establish a schedule.

The hash-free timing of tokio channel delivery and the actor's select_biased loop is unmeasured here; the 10 ms tick and 1 ms egress defaults in RuntimeConfig are configuration, not observed interleaving.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading gives a concrete mechanism. In InternalStorage::read, when from is below the compacted index the result is one create_compacted_entry element followed by one element per entry from compacted_idx to the requested end, so for from < compacted_idx the vector has fewer elements than decided_idx - from; the Trimmed(t)/Snapshotted variant is a marker for the whole trimmed prefix, not one index. The runtime stores only next_idx per subscriber, increments it once per element pushed (push_to_sub and push_to_all_subs), and push_to_all_subs computes start = sub.next_idx - min_next assuming one element per index. A subscription or catch-up at from < compacted therefore ends with next_idx = from + 1 + (decided - compacted), short of decided, and the next push re-reads from that cursor and re-sends entries after the compacted index. subscribe_decided accepts any from and documents a single in-order stream; nothing rejects or compensates for a compacted starting index. A Trimmed/Snapshotted marker is a documented LogEntry variant, so delivering it is not itself wrong; the defect is the cursor advance that treats the marker as one index.

interpretations.rationale: The pending completion path can report a false success, under a schedule the actor does not exclude. A pending append_notify keeps only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot). drain_notifiers evaluates, in order, Ok when assigned_idx <= decided, then Superseded when the assignment ballot is below the current promise ballot, then Timeout; the Ok arm reads no log entry and never checks that the value at assigned_idx is the caller's entry. The origin can hold an assignment made when it was leader or when a leader accepted its proposal, lose leadership to a higher ballot, and then have its own decided index advance past assigned_idx with a different value at that index: the runtime's own Superseded regression test constructs exactly that replacement (the old leader accepts locally with its outgoing cut, a new leader appends a fresh entry that decides at the same index, and the origin learns of the new ballot). Whether the pending resolves Ok or Superseded then depends only on whether a drain runs after the promise advanced but before decided reached assigned_idx. drain_notifiers runs only in the actor's tick branch; handling an incoming message never drains. Nothing orders a tick between the ballot change and the decided advance, so when the origin processes the higher-ballot Prepare and then the message that carries decided >= assigned_idx within one tick interval, the Ok arm wins and the caller is told its entry is decided at an index that holds a different entry. With a legal user-set tick_period that exceeds the leadership-turnover interval, that ordering is deterministic; with a short period it is a race. The gap on the reachable schedule is therefore answered on source grounds: no mechanism prevents it, and a legal configuration makes it the expected ordering.

3f84facd1a81451882518e32ee8be535-gap-0.explanation: Reachable. drain_notifiers is invoked only from the tick branch (actor.rs tick handling), while handle_incoming_tracked processes messages without draining; the actor polls the tick first each iteration but the tick fires at most once per configured period. The ballot change (Prepare/AcceptSync from the new leader) and the decided advance (AcceptDecide/Decide from that leader) are separate messages that can both be processed inside one period. If the period exceeds the turnover interval, the pending sees decided >= assigned_idx and a stale assignment ballot at the same drain, and the Ok arm precedes the Superseded arm. Since tick_period is user-set and only advised to match the ServerConfig tick budget, this ordering is legal and deterministic in that configuration.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes the mechanism but not yet the witness. handle_majority_promises sets the new leader's decided index to the maximum decided among the promises it has received (the prepare quorum); send_accsync then stamps every later promiser's AcceptSync with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which sets the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that promised during the prepare phase is part of that maximum; a follower whose Prepare is delayed until the leader is already in Accept is not, and set_promise for that later promise is called with check_max_prom false and does not update the maximum. If that follower had already learned a decision the quorum members had not, the AcceptSync lowers its decided index and read() reports a previously Decided entry as Undecided, contradicting the documented guarantee that a decided entry is not reverted and is safe to apply. The new leader then re-accepts and re-decides the entry after its accept quorum acknowledges, so the entry returns to Decided, exposing an at-least-once application hazard. The decisive uncertainty is whether the state can be built with real instances and legal message delays, which the registered five-node probe measures.
counterevidence: If the delayed follower's promise reaches the leader before the prepare quorum completes, its decided index participates in the maximum and no regression occurs.
If every member of the new leader's prepare quorum has also received the earlier Decide, the leader's decided index already covers the entry and the sync is not lowering anything.
The value of the entry is preserved by the sync, so this is a visibility and application-status defect rather than a divergence of decided values.

The fast subscriber is worse: push_to_all_subs reads from the trailing cursor 1, so the collapsed marker shifts every later element by compacted-1-min_next = 3 positions, and start = 6-1 = 5 lands on the last element, entry 10. The fast subscriber therefore receives entry 10 where it expected entry 7, then receives 8,9,10 on the next round; entry 7 is never delivered and entry 10 is delivered twice. Because the actor treats each pushed element as one committed log position, a single lagging subscriber silently corrupts the decided stream of every other subscriber. The root cause is the same as the earlier witness: the core read collapses a trimmed prefix into one element while the actor advances cursors and offsets fan-out by log index. A subscriber stream that silently omits a committed entry is a stronger violation of the documented in-order decided stream than duplicate delivery, and an application applying entries from the stream would miss entry 7 permanently.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes the mechanism but not yet the run. A node that accepts a StopSign stores it and increments its accepted index; once its decided index reaches that accepted index, stopsign_is_decided is true and is_reconfigured returns the StopSign. The reconnect path sends a Promise carrying that decided index, but the leader handles the late Promise in the Accept phase, where its AcceptSync is stamped with the leader's own decided index (which came from the prepare quorum and can be lower) and includes the StopSign it holds. sync_log then assigns the lower decided index while setting the StopSign, so decided < accepted and stopsign_is_decided becomes false; is_reconfigured returns None although the node previously reported the reconfiguration as decided. After the leader's accept quorum acknowledges, the StopSign is re-decided and is_reconfigured returns Some again. The consequence is an unstable authority-transition signal: a user polling is_reconfigured can observe a decided reconfiguration, then observe it as not decided. The probe measures whether the real instances realize this sequence.
counterevidence: If the new leader's prepare quorum already includes a node that decided the StopSign, the leader's decided index covers it and no flip occurs.
If the delayed node's Promise participates in the prepare quorum, its decided index enters the maximum and no flip occurs.
The StopSign itself is preserved across the sync, so the reconfiguration is not lost and the value at the index does not change; the defect is the transient status flip.
The new leader re-decides the StopSign after its accept quorum acknowledges, so the None window is bounded by one accept round.
limitations: No execution receipt yet.

The user's reaction to the flip is not modeled; only the observable is_reconfigured value is measured.
